title: design-qa.config.json
description: Per-repo configuration for the design-qa skill. String values may contain ${ENV_VAR} placeholders, expanded from the environment by scripts/capture.mjs (a missing variable is an error). Unknown keys are reported as warnings by scripts/validate.mjs, not errors.

baseUrl.errorMessage: must be an absolute http(s) URL or an environment-variable placeholder (a $ sign followed by {NAME})
baseUrl.description: Where the app runs, e.g. http://localhost:3000 or ${PREVIEW_URL}.

start.description: Command that starts the app locally (e.g. npm run dev).

readyUrl.description: Path or URL polled until the app answers.

storageState.description: PATH of a Playwright storage-state file a person saved by signing in themselves (scripts/setup.mjs save-session; default ~/.design-qa/sessions/<repo>-<host>.json). Never the session itself. ~ and ${ENV} are expanded; a relative path is relative to the config file. Used for auth type storageState when <envPrefix>_STORAGE_STATE is not set (the variable wins). The file must be outside the repository or git-ignored.

signedInSelector.description: CSS selector of an element only the signed-in app renders (the app shell's navigation, the user menu), present in every state. capture.mjs fails a state where it is not visible as a sign-in page (exit 6); when it is visible, the sign-in-form heuristics are skipped, so an app page with a password field (a settings screen) is never flagged.

signInUrlPattern.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) matched against the whole final URL of each state: a match that the planned URL does not have is a sign-in page (exit 6). For identity providers or sign-in routes the built-in heuristic misses.

figmaLibrary.errorMessage: must be a https://figma.com link (or an environment-variable placeholder), or null
figmaLibrary.description: Link to the design system's Figma library file: used to tell library components from lookalikes and to name variables. null: no library (asked once by setup.mjs).

tokens.description: Token files the design-system audit (scripts/ds-audit.mjs) checks every rendered value against, relative to this file: JSON (a { "--token": value } map, W3C design tokens with $value, Style Dictionary, a theme object exported to JSON) or CSS custom properties. A JS or TS theme is exported to JSON once.

libraries.description: Component libraries the design-system audit tells apart: the design system, raw third-party primitives and legacy components. An element belongs to the first library whose classPrefix or selector matches it.

classPrefix.description: A class name prefix that marks the library's elements (e.g. "Mui").

selector.description: A CSS selector that marks the library's elements (e.g. "[data-ds-component]").

wraps.description: design-system only: the name of the third-party library entry it is built on (same classes on the page). ds-audit then tells wrapper and raw use apart from the source: package (an npm name, or the wrapper's folder) is where the third-party library may be imported.

package.description: npm package name(s), for ds-audit.mjs --source: which local files import the library (a hint only).

items.errorMessage: needs a classPrefix or a selector to recognise the library's elements

commit.description: Whether reports in outDir are committed with the code (true) or kept out of git (false; outDir belongs in .gitignore). Asked once by setup.mjs; setup.mjs check reports a mismatch with .gitignore.

debtLog.errorMessage: must be the path of a Markdown file ending in .md (the JSON log is written next to it)
debtLog.description: Markdown design-debt log written by scripts/debt-log.mjs (the JSON log sits next to it, with .json for .md).

project.description: Project key for debt tickets when there is no parent issue.

parent.description: auto: the report's ticket (meta.ticket.key); null: no parent, use project.

allowNavigation.description: Do not fail states that end on another URL (an app that always redirects, say to a locale prefix or www); same as capture --allow-navigation. A state's own allowNavigation wins. Sign-in pages are still detected.

maxViewportHeight.description: Tallest design frame laid out at exactly W×H (default 1440, or 1000 for frames narrower than 768 px); a taller frame is laid out at W × maxViewportHeight so 100vh sections get a real screen height. It sets the layout viewport only: every capture covers the whole page. Same as capture --max-viewport-height.

viewportOnly.description: Opt-out: capture only the layout viewport (the old above-the-fold screenshot) instead of the whole page, for every state. Same as capture --viewport-only; a state's own viewportOnly wins. Rarely right: content below the fold is then never compared.

preCapture.description: Applied to every state of the app side before capture: storage set before the app's scripts run, elements hidden or removed with CSS, dismiss buttons clicked once if present. capture.json records the keys and selectors, never the storage values.

localStorage.description: Key → value set in localStorage before the page's scripts run (non-strings are JSON-encoded). A state's own storage wins on the same key.

sessionStorage.description: Key → value set in sessionStorage before the page's scripts run.

hide.description: Selectors made invisible (visibility: hidden): they keep their space in the layout.

remove.description: Selectors taken out of the layout (display: none) and removed from the DOM before the page is read.

click.description: Selectors clicked once, in order, when visible (a dismiss button); absent ones are skipped.

oneOf.description: A selector that applies only to the named states.

cssSelector.errorMessage: must be a CSS selector without { or }

route.description: Route template; may contain {id}/{fixture}, replaced by a state's fixture value.

fullPage.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored: every capture covers the whole page (see capture.viewportOnly for the opt-out).

preCapture.description: Merged over app.preCapture for this surface: its storage keys win, its selectors are added.

prototype.errorMessage: must be an http(s) or file: URL or an environment-variable placeholder (a $ sign followed by {NAME})
prototype.description: Prototype URL used as the design source of truth: a Figma prototype (figma.com/proto/...) or a coded prototype (Figma Make, Framer, v0, Lovable, static HTML, localhost). capture.mjs --side design captures it.

screens.description: Multi-screen surface: one entry per screen id (kebab-case, as in figma-fetch --screens auto). Each screen is captured with --screen <id> into evidence/screens/<id>.

figma.description: Figma link (design or proto) of this screen's frame.

prototype.errorMessage: must be an http(s) or file: URL or an environment-variable placeholder (a $ sign followed by {NAME})
prototype.description: Coded prototype URL of this screen.

route.description: App route of this screen (relative to app.baseUrl, or absolute).

driver.description: How to put the app into one state before capture. All keys optional; an empty object means the default render.

fixture.description: Replaces {fixture}/{id} in the route, otherwise appended as ?fixture=<value>.

query.description: Query string merged into the URL, e.g. ?state=empty or state=empty.

keys.description: Keys for action keyboard, space separated (Playwright names, e.g. Tab Tab Enter or Shift+Tab).

wait.description: Selector to wait for in this state (overrides capture --wait).

allowNavigation.description: The state may end on another URL (an action that navigates); otherwise a redirect or navigation away fails the state. Sign-in pages are still detected (see allowSignIn).

viewportOnly.description: Capture only the layout viewport for this state (true), or the whole page even when capture.viewportOnly is set (false).

allowSignIn.description: The state is meant to show a sign-in page (a sign-out flow, QA of the sign-in screen): skip sign-in detection for it.

source.description: Implemented in code but not drivable at runtime (file reference); the state is reported as CANNOT_VERIFY.
